source_note: Structured from the uploaded interview summary. Findings reflect one advisor interview and should not be treated as representative of all advisors.

themes.evidence_summary: Students frequently ask what to take next, whether courses count toward the degree, whether prerequisites are satisfied, and whether they are on track to graduate.
product_implications: Support semester course planning
Check prerequisite chains and course sequencing
Show how recommended courses satisfy degree requirements

themes.evidence_summary: Students struggle to connect broad fields such as applied math and data science to specific careers, skills, courses, projects, and experiences.
product_implications: Map target careers to required skills
Connect courses and projects to career goals
Provide career guidance earlier in the program

themes.evidence_summary: Advising information exists across multiple university pages and systems, which can create confusion and lead students to rely on peers.
product_implications: Provide a single interface for advising questions
Prefer official university sources
Display citations or source references with answers

themes.evidence_summary: Repeated questions include prerequisites, next-semester courses, remaining credits, elective eligibility, graduation timing, and unavailable required courses.
product_implications: Automate routine, rule-based advising questions
Use AI to prepare students before human advising meetings
Reserve advisor time for complex or individualized cases

themes.evidence_summary: Personal, unusual, high-impact, or exception-based decisions should involve a human advisor.
product_implications: Implement escalation to a human advisor
Avoid confident recommendations when uncertainty or exceptions are detected
Flag cases involving academic difficulty, major changes, withdrawals, transfer-credit issues, substitutions, or special approvals

themes.evidence_summary: Accurate advising requires both student-specific information and current university information.
The advisor considered citations and source explanations extremely important for trust, accountability, and error checking.
product_implications: Show the source used for prerequisite and degree-requirement decisions
Explain why a recommendation was made
Make it easy for students and advisors to verify AI outputs

themes.evidence_summary: Students often seek help only when registration is near or a problem already exists; earlier guidance could prevent issues.
product_implications: Send reminders about upcoming requirements
Warn students about prerequisite chains and limited course availability
Surface career-relevant suggestions before the final year

key_research_findings: Course planning is a major recurring advising need.
Career guidance should connect academic choices to skills and career paths earlier.
Routine advising questions are candidates for AI support, but complex exceptions require human judgment.
Source transparency and current institutional data are necessary for trustworthy recommendations.
The AI should support advisors rather than fully replace them.
limitations: This file represents one advisor interview.
The uploaded document is labeled as not completed.
The participant represents Applied Mathematics/Data Science and may not reflect other departments.
Product implications are interpretations and should be validated across additional interviews.
recommended_next_research_steps: Compare advisor findings with student survey results.
Promote recurring findings into validated product requirements only after multiple sources support them.
Create a use-case priority matrix using student demand, advisor support, impact, and technical feasibility.
